---
title: "Predict from a BayesA Fit"
---

## Predict from a BayesA Fit {.unnumbered}


### Description

Computes GEBVs and prediction metrics from a <code>run_bayesa</code>
fit. Behaviour and return value are identical to
<code>predict.masbayes_bayesr</code>; see that page for usage modes
and examples.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>## S3 method for class 'masbayes_bayesa'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, y_new = NULL, X_new = NULL, ...)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="object">object</code></td>
<td>
An object of class <code>masbayes_bayesa</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="newdata">newdata</code></td>
<td>
Optional numeric design matrix.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y_new">y_new</code></td>
<td>
Optional response vector for <code>newdata</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
Unused.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

An object of class <code>masbayes_prediction</code>.



### See Also

<code>run_bayesa</code>,
<code>summary.masbayes_bayesa</code>,
<code>predict.masbayes_bayesr</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

fit  <- run_bayesa(W_train, y_train, wtw_train, wty_train,
                   sigma2_g      = var(y_train)/2,
                   sigma2_e_init = var(y_train)/2)
pred <- predict(fit, W_test, y_test)
pred$metrics$AUC      # for binary traits




```
